comment_regular_data.body: got to it like 10s before me LOL

I'm still opposed to this; I think the consistency here is worth it over an extra feature. Plus, typing `:e .` pretty quick.

Plus (to me), it doesn't make sense as a variant of `-`. If `-` is "open parent directory", what is the current directory a parent of when using `1-`?

> what is the current directory a parent of when using `1-`?

all buffers/windows/tabs have an "effective CWD", that's what `1-` acts upon.



> I think the consistency here is worth it over an extra feature.

why? `1-` does nothing useful otherwise.

and this is a pattern i think should be considered in more places; as i mentioned, it is the normal-mode equivalent of the bang "!" concept.

if we choose not to use this, we're just choosing to ignore that opportunity...

I just realized something really obvious, btw.

`1-` is not like `[count]-`. The former is ALWAYS the filesystem dir provider; the latter can use the provider for the buf.

See new code

EDIT: agree with justin also

> `1-` is not like `[count]-`.

Yeah, that inconsistency is my main issue with it.

> > what is the current directory a parent of when using `1-`?
> 
> all buffers/windows/tabs have an "effective CWD", that's what `1-` acts upon.

Got it! That works well for the metaphor. I'll sleep better at night :)

> and this is a pattern i think should be considered in more places; as i mentioned, it is the normal-mode equivalent of the bang "!" concept.

Not the biggest fan right now, but I suppose I'll get used to it once it starts appearing in more places. From a practical perspective it's definitely a useful tool to have. LGTM! (once it's ready ofc)
